scenes.title: INNER JOIN
scenes.narration: An INNER JOIN combines rows from two tables and keeps only the pairs that match on a shared key.

scenes.title: What INNER JOIN does
bullets: Returns only rows that have a match in both tables.
Requires an ON clause naming the join key.
Rows with no match on either side are excluded.
scenes.narration: It returns only rows that have a match in both tables, so unmatched records simply disappear. You must supply an ON clause naming the columns that link the tables. Because the match must exist on both sides, any row without a partner is dropped from the result.

scenes.title: How the join is evaluated
steps: Take each row from the left table.
Look for rows in the right table where ON is true.
Emit one combined row per matching pair.
Discard rows that found no match.
scenes.narration: The engine walks each left-side row and searches the right table for rows where the ON condition is true. For every matching pair it emits one combined row, and any row that finds no partner is discarded.

scenes.title: Employees with their department
scenes.code:
SELECT e.name, e.salary, d.dept_name
FROM employees AS e
INNER JOIN departments AS d
  ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;
scenes.narration: Here we join employees to departments on the shared dept_id column. Each employee row is paired with the matching department, so we can select the employee's name and salary alongside the department name. An employee whose dept_id has no matching department, or a department with no employees, is excluded from the output.

scenes.title: Filtering after the join
scenes.code:
SELECT c.customer_name, o.order_id, o.amount
FROM customers AS c
INNER JOIN orders AS o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.amount > 100
ORDER BY o.amount DESC;
scenes.narration: This joins customers to their orders, then keeps only the joined rows where the order amount exceeds one hundred. Customers with no orders never appear because an inner join requires a match on both sides. The WHERE clause filters the matched result, and ORDER BY sorts the largest orders first.

scenes.title: INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN

left.title: INNER JOIN
points: Never produces NULLs from missing matches.

right.title: LEFT JOIN
points: Fills right columns with NULL when unmatched.
Preserves rows an inner join would drop.

scenes.narration: An inner join is symmetric and returns only the intersection of matches, never inventing NULLs. A left join instead preserves every left row, padding the right-side columns with NULL when no match is found. Choose inner when unmatched rows are irrelevant.

scenes.text: Reach for INNER JOIN when you only care about records that exist in both tables and unmatched rows can be safely ignored.
scenes.narration: Use an inner join whenever you only care about records present in both tables and unmatched rows can be safely ignored.
